clause: Applies RETROACTIVELY: every held corpus either flows to a surface, stages promotion-ready, or carries an ARGUED reason it cannot (three dispositions, no fourth; 'we acquired it' is not one of the three).
quote: Held data with no live promotion tail is a defect. While unattended promotion is OFF, the pipeline still runs to a STAGED, promotion-ready state and session shipping carries the last mile.
reason: Both live dispositions are carried by R-0248 clause 7 (flows to a surface = surface reflects truth or renders the honest gap; stages promotion-ready = STAGED state). The one-time retroactive sweep is spent, and the 'argued reason it cannot' escape valve is a softening the stricter successor legitimately drops (an escape-valve permission is not an obligation/bar).

clause: The complete applicable universe is PER AUTHORITY, not per state; a corpus must state WHAT IT IS NOT, and every item in that list is an absence from a DOCUMENT, never an absence from a ballot.
quote: Where an authority governs a state, acquire the state; where it governs a county, municipality or district, acquire that authority's complete applicable universe.
reason: Per-authority denominator is carried verbatim by R-0248 clause 6. 'State what it is not' is carried by R-0254 ('three numbers are reported: rendering, deliberately out of scope and why, and in scope and still dark'). Document-absence vs ballot-absence is the bedrock of R-0250 (a branch returning empty is one measurement, never a verdict about the fact) and R-0254's whose-gap naming.

clause: The safe default is under-claiming: the label is classified from a register where each acquisition is declared beside the run that earned it, anything undeclared is PILOT_DERIVED, and a label that can only be earned cannot be inherited.
quote: A tier is never inferred at read time and never raised by a session that did not do the work. Census and NCES establish Tiers 0 and 1; they never establish Tier 2.
reason: The earned-label-cannot-be-inherited bar is carried by R-0275 (a tier is never inferred, never raised without the work). The under-claim default (undeclared = pilot-derived) is carried by R-0248 clause 6 ('a pilot-derived population is labelled pilot-derived'); the register-of-declared-acquisitions is R-0252's evidence-cited write path and R-0263's sources register.

clause: The session reports how many further bodies the branch then reached, as a pair against how many were hand-worked; a hand-worked body that produced one row and no branch has spent the discovery and kept nothing.
quote: Where no automated branch reaches a body, the session hand-works it — that is the job, not a fallback — and the branch it builds becomes project property inherited by every later body, ZIP and state.
reason: The load-bearing bar (hand-work must yield a reusable branch, not one throwaway row) is carried by R-0248 clause 8. The reached-vs-hand-worked pair is a reporting-instrumentation detail subsumed by R-0253's required EXPANSION section (how each route was conceived, what it returned, where else it applies).

clause: When a branch fails somewhere new it is not discarded — it grows a sub-branch, and the failure is recorded with the jurisdiction and the date.
quote: A method write cites its evidence: artifact, route, jurisdiction, vendor context, observed date, and the disposition that earned it. ... A rejected candidate is retained as rejected.
reason: Never-discarded + recorded-with-jurisdiction-and-date is carried by R-0252 (rejected candidate retained; evidence cites jurisdiction and observed date). The 'grows a sub-branch' (learn the new jurisdictional shape) is R-0248 clause 8 (the branch becomes project property inherited by every later body) plus R-0252's new-validated-method reopening.

clause: Every run reports branches INHERITED against branches NEWLY BUILT as a pair; a session that builds a branch which already existed has committed a defect and reports it as one, naming the existing branch; a new branch is checked against the manifest BEFORE it is built (duplication is worse than a gap).
quote: Every later session inherits method knowledge and none re-derives it, so a wrong sentence in the store costs every session after it.
reason: The anti-duplication bar (check before build; don't re-derive an existing branch) is carried by R-0252's 'none re-derives it' and its one-governed-write-path that validates before writing. The inherited-vs-built pair is a reporting detail subsumed by R-0253's EXPANSION section.

clause: An inherited branch that fails in a new jurisdiction grows a sub-branch per RULING 60, is never deleted, and its failure is recorded with the jurisdiction and the date.
quote: A rejected candidate is retained as rejected. ... A method write cites its evidence: artifact, route, jurisdiction, vendor context, observed date, and the disposition that earned it.
reason: Same sub-branch-on-failure obligation as the R-0060 clause: retained-not-deleted with jurisdiction and date is R-0252; the sub-branch growth is R-0248 clause 8 (branch becomes inherited project property).

clause: A failed inherited route is also knowledge: it grows a sub-branch naming the jurisdictional shape it failed in and the date, and is never deleted.
quote: A rejected candidate is retained as rejected.
reason: Third assertion of the same obligation. R-0252 keeps the failed route as retained knowledge with its evidence (jurisdiction, observed date); R-0248 clause 8 and R-0252's new-validated-method mechanism carry the shape-learning that grows the sub-branch.

clause: A new jurisdiction is PRESUMED CAPABLE of teaching the project a new method; 'nothing new learned' is legitimate only after genuine expansion work occurred and may never be inferred merely because all inherited routes completed.
quote: Every hunt report carries an EXPANSION section listing routes that did not exist at session start ... In every hunt brief it is its own numbered item and never last.
reason: The bar against false convergence is carried by R-0253's required EXPANSION section (a hunt must produce new routes; walking the inherited list is not enough) reinforced by R-0252's versioned convergence ('never that no other source exists') and R-0248 clause 8 ('the method learned so far, never the method').

clause: Where a body is REQUIRED to publish and has not, that is a finding rendered as one, and it carries an EVIDENCE STANDARD (specific publication obligation; authoritative source cited; why it applies to this body and document type; effective/applicable date; date checked; complete retrieval history; final failed state), never upgraded to a compliance claim where the obligation is uncertain, and no claim without a source record.
quote: Affirmative source-backed evidence about the record itself — not created, not yet published, lawfully withheld, destroyed under retention, not obtainable publicly — where our failure to retrieve is never that evidence.
reason: The load-bearing bar (a non-publication finding requires affirmative source-backed evidence about the record, never our own failed retrieval) is carried by R-0248 clause 2(b), and the VERIFIED_ABSENT evidence discipline is R-0250 (routes walked/named/dated + stuck protocol). 'No claim without a source record' is R-0255 ('if none exists, the field is null'). The seven-part evidence enumeration is operational detail of that standard.

clause: The ladder has FOURTEEN rungs (the specific count and enumeration that walledAtRung integers reference).
quote: The retrieval-mechanics ladder in CLAUDE.md is canonical and its numbering is what reaches the database as walledAtRung.
reason: References the numbered retrieval-mechanics ladder / rung enumeration, which is being repaired separately under R-0249.

clause: Every session reports rungs added and where they landed.
quote: Only a genuinely new retrieval class adds a rung.
reason: References the numbered ladder (rungs added). The rung-add mechanism is R-0249 (ladder repair in progress); the session-reporting duty is also carried by R-0253's EXPANSION section (new routes conceived, what they returned, whether recorded).

clause: Wikipedia gives ROSTER depth, not KELLY depth: photos, phones and campaign sites are still hunted after it.
quote: The Kelly standard is the definition of done per candidate — photo, phone, working contact, specific verified page, campaign site — with no tiers.
reason: Roster is not done; the deeper fields are still owed is carried by R-0255 (Kelly standard = done) and R-0275 (Tier 0 roster only vs Tier 3 Kelly depth; a tier is never raised without the work). Wikipedia-as-discovery-only is R-0249 ('a discovery source, never a source of record').

clause: The directory is walked before the tier below it is hunted, and the enumeration it produces is reconciled against the official universe as a PAIR, never blended; two official enumerations that disagree is a FINDING (RULING 57).
quote: Coverage descends. Each tier publishes the tier beneath it, and a tier is not complete until the tier above has been asked what is in it. ... A total that reconciles is not a total that is correct.
reason: Directory-before-tier-below is R-0251's descend-from-the-tier-above rule (a body found only by per-entity search when the tier above was never asked is a coverage defect). Reconcile-never-blend is R-0251 ('A total that reconciles is not a total that is correct', checked externally against Census/NCES). Two-enumerations-disagree-keep-both is entailed by R-0250's absence-never-asserted (a body one authority lists is never dropped).

clause: An invalid key opens a Needs Sean P1 row the same session.
quote: An access escalation is a parallel lane, never a stop. Where a token, account, export, feed or quota would materially help, name it precisely ... A decision that is genuinely the author's becomes a row and the session keeps going.
reason: Invalid-key detection is R-0249 ('A credential is proven by calling it, never assumed'); the same-session owner escalation is R-0271's access-escalation lane (name it, open the row, keep working). The specific P1 priority is subsumed by R-0270's generic three-level priority scale.

clause: Tier A splits into A0 (the body's own publication and the tier above it in government; bulk download first, then the body's own pages; RULING 93's directory lives here) and A1 (third-party compilations — Wikipedia, LegiScan, Citizens Count, Open States, GovTrack — still Tier A, walked after A0); B and C unchanged.
quote: Tier A0 — the body's own publication, bulk download first. The governing body that holds the office is walked before any aggregator, and where it offers a bulk file the bulk file is taken before any page-by-page retrieval.
reason: R-0249 keeps the ordered A0/A/B/C ladder and the body's-own-before-aggregator order. The A1 sub-label is folded into Tier A (a structural relabel, not an obligation change); the descend-from-the-tier-above ordering the directory needs is independently guaranteed by R-0251 regardless of A0/A placement.

clause: A bulk file is rung ZERO because it is not a retrieval problem at all (the fourteen mechanics rungs are about getting bytes past a wall; a published .txt roster has no wall).
quote: where it offers a bulk file the bulk file is taken before any page-by-page retrieval.
reason: Defines 'rung zero' against the fourteen numbered mechanics rungs; the numbered ladder is being repaired separately under R-0249. The bulk-file-first obligation itself is carried by R-0249 Tier A0.

clause: The fourteen numbered mechanics rungs and their meanings (committed snapshot; plain fetch; full browser headers; different TLS client; different egress; live browser with JS; page's own network calls; structured markup; linked documents in every format; sitemaps/caches; Internet Archive; vendor platform; public-records request; author's browser last).
quote: The retrieval-mechanics ladder in CLAUDE.md is canonical and its numbering is what reaches the database as walledAtRung.
reason: This IS the numbered retrieval-mechanics ladder definition, being repaired separately under R-0249.

clause: A hunt is over only when every rung below has been walked and recorded with attemptedAt and its result.
quote: A move that was refused by a wall still counts as walked, carrying its rung history and test date.
reason: The exhaustion standard is tied to the numbered ladder ('every rung below'), which is being repaired under R-0249. The walked-and-recorded-with-date-and-result discipline is independently carried by R-0250 (every route walked, named and dated; a walled move still counts as walked with its rung history and test date).

clause: Every session reports RUNGS ADDED and where they landed (which existing rung was enriched, or which number was added for a new class); a run that learned a new way past a wall and did not write it down has kept nothing.
quote: Only a genuinely new retrieval class adds a rung.
reason: References the numbered ladder (rungs added), repaired under R-0249. The write-it-down-or-keep-nothing reporting duty is also carried by R-0253's EXPANSION section and R-0252 ('a wrong sentence in the store costs every session after it').

clause: Not reaching a required input is a fault to REPORT, never a permitted/acceptable outcome; a brief may not pre-authorize skipping an unreachable input.
quote: An operation that can return nothing is asked what it returned. A zero-row extraction is a failed extraction, never an empty document. ... A failed fetch never silently empties a previously full surface.
reason: An unreachable/empty required input is a reported failure, never a silent acceptable outcome: R-0269 (nothing returned is a failure, asked what it returned) plus R-0250 ('missing tooling is not absence') and R-0273 (stop only when the environment actually prevents continuation, recording a stop_reason). A brief cannot pre-authorize a skip: R-0253 ('A brief may add to it and never subtract') and R-0272 authority precedence (a brief that conflicts with law does not silently win).

clause: A file write that removes assertions from an existing test file FAILS THE BUILD unless the removal is explicit and intentional; the guard census fails BY NAME, and guard:census --write refuses to erase a name without --allow-removals.
quote: A test file may not lose assertions silently.
reason: The substantive bar (silent loss of test assertions fails) is carried verbatim by R-0267 ('the suite asserts checks registered equal checks reporting. A test file may not lose assertions silently'). The guard-census-by-name and the --allow-removals flag are the operational mechanism of that bar.

clause: CLAUSE 1 — Evidence is the checked kind or it is not evidence: an instrument may not accept, as evidence for its own conclusion, an input it has not itself checked; a declared input may be reported or carried as a hypothesis, never the thing a verdict rests on.
quote: An instrument may not accept, as evidence for its own conclusion, an input it has not itself checked. A guard that restates a declaration in a stronger voice is worse than no guard.
reason: Carried verbatim in the R-0267 opening. The declared-input-as-hypothesis half is reinforced by R-0272 ('A session's reading is recorded as a reading ... neither becomes the rule by being written confidently') and R-0252 (model statements recorded as claims, never durable provenance).

clause: CLAUSE 2 — A denominator is not a membership proof: cardinality is a diagnostic; two sets of equal size are not the same set; a gate that cannot name the elements has not compared them.
restoreText: A count is a diagnostic, not a membership proof: two sets of equal size are not the same set, and a gate that cannot name the elements it compared has not compared them.
reason: A distinct instrument proof-standard squarely in R-0274's theme, carried nowhere in the 32-ruling corpus. R-0274 has 'a reconciliation names its external anchor' (names the anchor, not the elements) and 'a guard may pin an invariant ... never the size of a gap'; R-0269's conservation equation is extraction accounting; R-0254's 'Stated N equals rendered rows' requires the equality this clause warns is insufficient for membership; R-0275's 'identical payloads across distinct keys are presumed a collapse' is payload-level. None states cardinality-is-not-membership or 'name the elements.' This is the protection behind the ballot defect (a certified count equal to a rendered count does not prove the same candidate set) and has no retirement justification.

clause: CLAUSE 3 — Unknown semantics fails closed: where a rule's applicability depends on a property not established for the case at hand, the answer is the WEAKER claim; the default for anything unclassified is the weaker claim; a new case may not inherit the strong sentence by silence.
quote: A tier is never inferred at read time and never raised by a session that did not do the work.
reason: The fail-closed-to-the-weaker-claim principle is pervasively instantiated across the live corpus: R-0275 (a tier/label is never inferred, never raised without the work; identical payloads presumed a collapse until proven distinct), R-0248 clause 6 (undeclared population labelled pilot-derived), R-0249/R-0250 (unconfirmed is a LEAD not a FOUND; CANNOT_TELL fails safe; a guessed identifier yields a LEAD not a HIT), and R-0267/R-0274 (a check that cannot run says so; silence is not a passing result). No case inherits the strong sentence by silence.

clause: EARLY_HANDOFF is required when capacity and executable work remain and the session closes anyway; do not convert preservation quality into permission to stop.
quote: Every non-complete close records a specific stop_reason and executable_owed_work_remaining, derived from canonical state by pnpm workstream:close, never asserted. An external stop is never inferred; one blocked item never qualifies while other work exists.
reason: EARLY_HANDOFF is one of the five statuses and its trigger is derived, not chosen: a voluntary close with executable work remaining and no genuine external stop is EARLY_HANDOFF. Because executable_owed_work_remaining is derived and never asserted, and stopping is lawful only when complete, redirected, or actually prevented, a well-preserved handoff cannot self-award a clean stop — which is exactly 'preservation quality is not permission to stop.'

clause: MERGE CADENCE IS NOT SESSION CADENCE: the planned merge having occurred is not a legitimate reason to stop; delay the merge until the session is actually ready to end.
quote: Merge cadence is not session cadence. The planned merge having happened is never a reason to stop.
reason: Carried verbatim by R-0266 (the prior auditor, seeing only the session-domain successor, missed that shipping-CI R-0266 carries it). 'Delay the merge until the session is ready to end' is R-0266's 'accumulate the session's work, ship one planned code merge at the real end.'

clause: PERSISTED RESUMABILITY IS NOT PERMISSION TO STOP VOLUNTARILY: canonical state exists so an interrupted session can resume, not so this one can end.
quote: When capacity actually ends, the only lawful output is UNFINISHED SESSION with the exact resume point and every unreached item by name — and that is not a failure.
reason: R-0273 frames the exact resume point as the output produced only WHEN CAPACITY ACTUALLY ENDS — resumability is a consequence of a genuine stop, not a cause of one. Combined with 'KEEP WORKING WHILE AUTHORIZED EXECUTABLE WORK REMAINS' and the three lawful stop conditions, a voluntary stop justified by saved state is already forbidden (it becomes EARLY_HANDOFF). Restoring a separate sentence would duplicate R-0273's core, which R-0247 forbids.

clause: A subagent's report of 'done' is not inspection; the lead owns truth, coordination, conflict resolution and full-product validation.
quote: The adversarial auditor starts from the publisher, the canonical identity and the vault — never from the original worker's summary.
reason: Do-not-trust-the-worker's-summary is carried verbatim by R-0274. The lead-owns-validation half is R-0266 ('Branch-local green is necessary and never sufficient; only the integrated head ships; the integration owner alone reconciles the shared stores') and R-0273 ('a paragraph is not a contract'; interfaces proven by a compatibility test running the real producer into the real consumer).

clause: Designate one integration/release owner; one combined head, one merge at the end; the integration owner alone reconciles shared stores and regenerates generated artifacts once.
quote: One integration owner, one combined head, one merge at the end. ... the integration owner alone reconciles the shared stores — canonical work state, the tracker, state and log, the method store — and regenerates every generated artifact once.
reason: Carried verbatim by R-0266 (and echoed in CLAUDE.md line 142).

clause: Correctness still outranks speed; the goal is maximum safe parallel throughput not maximum branches; two branches independently rewriting one canonical store or regenerating one output are refused.
quote: One session at a time touches shared infrastructure — scheduler, refresh, schema, ops. Reader-surface sessions run in parallel with anything.
reason: Correctness-outranks-speed is R-0273 ('Correct first. Fast second. Nothing third.'). The safety bound on parallelism (two branches may not independently rewrite one canonical store or regenerate one output) is carried by R-0277 (one session at a time on shared infrastructure) and R-0266 (the integration owner alone reconciles shared stores and regenerates each artifact once).

clause: A declared dependency is PROVEN only by a mechanical fact (owned-domain overlap or a produces/consumes handoff); a prose-only edge is UNPROVEN; independent, executable and serialized is a FAILURE.
quote: serializing them is a defect that must name the dependency ... Any interface between independently built lanes is one shared typed schema imported by both sides and proven by a compatibility test that runs the real producer into the real consumer; a paragraph is not a contract.
reason: Independent-executable-serialized-is-a-failure and prose-is-not-proof are carried by R-0273. The mechanical dependency-proof standard (owned-domain overlap / produces-consumes handoff) is enforced by the orchestration:check instrument, which R-0267 names as a required gate ('governance:check, orchestration:check and method:check are in that set by name'); R-0272 confirms a rule lives in its instrument.

clause: The counts are reported separately (FIXED_VERIFIED / OPEN_EXECUTABLE / NEEDS_OWNER); only OPEN_EXECUTABLE reaching zero completes a session's scoped work.
quote: NEEDS_OWNER is terminal for the session's denominator and never counts as open executable work.
reason: The load-bearing rule (NEEDS_OWNER is not executable, so only executable work reaching zero completes scoped work) is carried verbatim by R-0273. The separate-count reporting is subsumed by R-0273's derived executable_owed_work_remaining and R-0262's 'every ending carries its denominator ... N of M closed.'

clause: The govern verb does not attach: name the nation, its government and its meetings, but do not assert a governing relationship (tribal jurisdiction turns on membership and land status, not geography).
quote: Show-everything guarantees completeness within the correct scope; it never licenses displaying an entity that does not govern the reader.
reason: Name-the-nation is R-0251/R-0275 ('A sovereign tribal nation is its own category of government ... with its own label and body class, nationally'). Do-not-assert-a-governing-relationship is R-0256 (never displaying an entity that does not govern the reader; a tribal nation intersecting a ZIP does not govern the reader because governance is membership/land-based, not geographic). The membership-vs-geography rationale is the WHY and lives in history per R-0247.
